WHAT YOU’RE SEEING

A LITTLE EXPERIMENT

Make two waves disappear.

Set the phase difference to 180°. The equal waves oppose each other at every point, so their sum is zero in this ideal model.

Inside this model +

Two waves of equal amplitude and frequency travel in the same direction. Their displacements add: y = A sin(kx − ωt) + A sin(kx − ωt + φ).

The resultant amplitude is 2A |cos(φ/2)|. At 0° the waves reinforce; at 180° they cancel. The model assumes ideal linear waves of equal amplitude. Cancellation of displacement is not a claim that energy vanishes in a physical source system.

Wave speed is fixed at 2 m/s, so wavelength λ = v/f. Phase is in degrees, time in seconds, and displacement in centimetres. Explore more with PhET’s Wave Interference ↗
